raw_response:
I will keep all 3.0 mu in stevia this year. My land is small, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but I still do not want to be stingy and lose leaf yield. What I do is start from what worked before and only adjust a little. For stevia, I will use improved seedlings again, because the newer ones usually stand more evenly and the leaf comes out cleaner if water is steady. I have well irrigation, so I will not let the field stay dry for long after transplanting. On fertilizer, I will put most of it in before planting, then topdress nitrogen later after the plants catch hold and after the first strong growth starts. I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because if stevia stays pale and weak early, it is hard to make that yield back. Potash matters too, because the stems need to stay strong and the leaves need to build well. Since my farm is only 3 mu and some family members work off-farm, I will keep the plan simple: rotary tillage, steady water, and a few pesticide sprays when insects or leaf disease start showing. Around here, I will mostly do close to what experienced growers do, just a little cleaner on timing because I can manage a small field carefully.
